chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: Hearing New Orleans bands on trips; Bolden his favorite
summary: Before moving he visited on Mondays to hear Clem, Bolden and Robichaux, and Bolden was his favorite.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: So when you were 21 years old you came to New Orleans, huh?

To live, yeah. But I, after, I bought my first good horn, then I, I felt like I wanted to go to New Orleans, you know, the 90th century, you know, to go there. Yes. So I'd go on weekends, I mean, on Mondays, I'd work Sundays, sometime I'd go through, wouldn't stop in the process, go to catch the dance on Monday at a lawn party, you know. In New Orleans? Yeah, the other bands play.
Did you listen to a lot of the other bands?
Yeah, it was Clem, Bolin, and... Clem had a band, huh? Yeah. Was he a cleft player? Trumpet. He was kind of blind, like, you know.
Mm-hmm. Robichaux was the other one?
Three brothers. Johnny, Ed, and... What's the other bass player there? I've forgotten his name.
The old dad. What was your favorite band, then, when you were going into town, like, once in a while, like that? Uh...
Bolin was my favorite band. Bolin.
And Robichaux. What was your favorite?
